He played college basketball for the [[University of Georgia]]. A 6’7” [[power forward]] from [[Pontiac, Michigan]], Maten won [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]] by the [[Associated Press]] as a senior. ==College career== After starring at [[Lahser High School]] for three years until its closure in 2013, and then in the 2013–14 season at its successor, [[Bloomfield Hills High School]], Maten surprised recruiting experts by selecting [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]] over [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] and home state school [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]].{{cite news|last1=Carvell|first1=Michael|title=The story behind UGA's big recruiting victory|url=http://recruiting.blog.ajc.com/2014/04/09/the-story-behind-ugas-big-recruiting-victory/|access-date=January 13, 2018|work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|date=April 14, 2014}} After a breakout sophomore year where he was named second-team All-[[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) by the league's coaches, Maten enjoyed a strong individual junior season, marred by a knee injury and the Bulldogs’ mediocre 19–14 record.{{cite news|last1=Paschall|first1=David|title=Georgia's Yante Maten out indefinitely with knee sprain|url=http://www.timesfreepress.com/news/sports/college/story/2017/feb/20/georgias-maten-out-indefinitely-knee-sprain/413735/|access-date=January 13, 2018|work=[[Chattanooga Times Free Press]]|date=February 27, 2017}} After averaging 18.2 points and 6.8 rebounds per game, he was named first-team All-SEC by the leagues’ coaches and second-team by the [[Associated Press]]. He was also named as a finalist for the [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar Award]] for the nation's top [[Center (basketball)|center]] (despite starting the season on the watch list for the [[Karl Malone Award]] for top power forward).{{cite news|title=Georgia junior Yante Maten a finalist for Abdul-Jabbar award|url=http://onlineathens.com/sports/2017-02-03/georgia-junior-yante-maten-finalist-abdul-jabbar-award|access-date=January 13, 2018|work=[[Athens Banner-Herald]]|date=February 3, 2017}} Following his junior season, Maten declared his eligibility for the [[2017 NBA draft]] without an agent, leaving open the possibility of returning to Georgia for his senior year.{{cite news|title=Georgia junior forward Yante Maten submits for draft without agent|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19149731/yante-maten-georgia-bulldogs-submits-name-nba-draft|access-date=January 13, 2018|work=[[ESPN.com]]|date=April 13, 2017}} Ultimately, after working out for NBA teams he decided to return to Georgia for his senior year to improve his draft position.{{cite news|last1=Carvell|first1=Michael|title=The story behind UGA's big recruiting victory|url=http://recruiting.blog.ajc.com/2014/04/09/the-story-behind-ugas-big-recruiting-victory/|access-date=January 13, 2018|work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|date=April 14, 2014}} Prior to the start of the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18 season]], Maten was named the preseason SEC co-Player of the Year (with [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]] forward [[Robert Williams III|Robert Williams]] and incoming [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]] freshman [[Michael Porter Jr.]]).{{cite news|last1=Butt|first1=Jason|title=Maten shares preseason honor at SEC Men's Basketball Media Day|url=http://www.macon.com/sports/college/university-of-georgia/bulldogs-beat/uga-football/article179472756.html|access-date=January 13, 2018|work=[[The Telegraph (Macon)|The Telegraph]]|date=October 18, 2017}} After a strong start to the season,{{cite news|title=UGA roundup: Yante Maten named SEC Player of the Week|url=http://onlineathens.com/dogbytes/sports/2017-12-26/uga-roundup-yante-maten-named-sec-player-week|access-date=January 13, 2018|work=[[Athens Banner-Herald]]|date=December 26, 2017}} Maten was named to the [[John R. Wooden Award]] midseason top 25 watch list on January 10, one of only two SEC players to be so recognized.{{cite news|last1=Knapp|first1=Corey|title=Georgia's Yante Maten makes Wooden Award midseason top 25|url=http://www.ajc.com/sports/college/georgia-yante-maten-makes-wooden-award-midseason-top/j701rIMXiwUMxayrhBfbhI/|access-date=January 13, 2018|work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|date=January 11, 2018|archive-date=January 14, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180114020225/http://www.ajc.com/sports/college/georgia-yante-maten-makes-wooden-award-midseason-top/j701rIMXiwUMxayrhBfbhI/|url-status=dead}} Maten won [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]] by the [[Associated Press]] and was named to the All-SEC First Team. ==Professional career== ===Miami Heat (2018–2019)=== After not being selected in the [[2018 NBA draft]], Maten signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Miami Heat]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) on July 29, 2018. Under the terms of the deal, he split his time between the Heat and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].{{cite news|title=Heat Signs Yante Maten|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-yante-maten|access-date=July 29, 2018|work=[[NBA.com]]|date=July 29, 2018}} On December 2, 2018, Maten scored a career-high 42 points to go along with 14 rebounds and 3 blocks in a 113–108 win over the Stockton Kings.{{cite web|url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/game/2021800151/|title=Sioux Falls Skyforce 113 - Stockton Kings 108|publisher=G League Stats|date=December 2, 2018|access-date=June 20, 2020}} Maten was named NBA G League Player of the Month for December 2018.{{cite web|title=Yante Maten Named G League Player Of The Month|date=January 2, 2019|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/252106/Yante-Maten-Named-G-League-Player-Of-The-Month|access-date=January 2, 2019}} On April 7, 2019, the Heat signed Maten to a standard NBA contract.{{cite web|title=HEAT Signs Yante Maten|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-yante-maten-190407|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 7, 2019|date=April 7, 2019}} On July 29, 2019, Maten was waived by the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite news|title=Heat Waives Yante Maten|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-waives-yante-maten|access-date=July 29, 2019|work=NBA.com|date=July 29, 2019}} ===Maine Red Claws (2019–2020)=== On September 17, 2019, Maten was reported to have signed with the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|first1=Quenton|last1=Albertie|title=Report: Celtics sign forward Yante Maten to Exhibit 10 deal|url=https://celticswire.usatoday.com/2019/09/17/report-celtics-sign-forward-yante-maten-to-exhibit-10-deal|date=September 17, 2019|work=usatoday.com|access-date=September 17, 2019|archive-date=October 14, 2019, Maten was reported to have waived by the Celtics.{{cite web|title=The Celtics waive Maten|url=https://www.usbasket.com/NBA/news/598739/The-Celtics-waive-Maten|date=October 20, 2019|work=usbasket.com|access-date=October 20, 2019}} On October 26, 2019, Maten was included in the training camp roster of the [[Maine Red Claws]].{{cite web|first1=Evans|last1=Boston|title=2019 NBA G League Draft RED CLAWS DRAFT FOUR, ANNOUNCE TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/2019-draft|date=October 26, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 26, joined [[Wonju DB Promy]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]] for the 2020–21 season.{{Cite web|title=Former Bulldogs Begin Professional Seasons
